topic: Project Northstar Week 3 interim steering decision
source_policy: Use only local Project Northstar source documents, reproduced processed outputs, and explicitly labelled analyst judgments. Keep screens, diagnostic samples, proposed targets, and client-approved facts visually distinct. Every slide carries compact sources; full file-level provenance and caveats remain in speaker notes and the Markdown source.

items.claim: Federated coordination should advance only as a conditional design direction; local stabilization remains the fallback and global coordination is held.
items.evidence_label: ANALYST-JUDGMENT, with ACG-DATA for the FY2026 ceiling
items.boundary: No execution, funding, cash movement, closure, labor action, benefit, or spend approval.

items.claim: Reporting and payment friction is concentrated in observable source and cohort patterns, while cash mobility, causes, and removability remain unproved.
items.boundary: $38.13m is a 30 June 14-day screen, not cash; the 7,600 records are a supplied extract, not a certified enterprise population.

items.claim: Federated scores 87 versus 72 local and 60 global, leads all five declared sensitivities, and remains subordinate to seven non-compensating gates.
items.boundary: The weighted score is not confidence, value, execution readiness, or client approval.

items.claim: The proposed federated operating model couples one global data/control spine with explicit regional and local validation, emergency, and execution rights.
items.boundary: The model does not select a platform, bank, vendor, architecture, or production process.

items.claim: A controlled 55-account census must precede any later 10-account read-only visibility test, with AC0040 protected through enhanced review.
items.boundary: The cohort is purposive and not launch-ready; the pilot has no mobility or value KPI.

items.claim: The payment v3 design selects 120 records across four strata using 8 exception/status issues, 7 late-only issues, and 15 controls per stratum, producing 50 exact pairs and 10 visible deviations.
items.boundary: Purposive case-control diagnosis only; not prevalence, causation, benefit, capacity, or enterprise extrapolation.

items.claim: Cash release, annual P&L, productive capacity, and risk are separate non-additive ledgers; all recognized value is $0 and risk exposure/value is not quantified.
items.boundary: Do not total the ledgers; actual cost, ROI, NPV, payback, and funding recommendation are unavailable.

items.claim: The manager downside preserves the conditional federated design direction, but failures in ownership, integration readiness, affordability, or a critical gate force a switch or redesign.
items.boundary: The downside does not make the option investable; validated value remains $0 and cost remains unavailable.

items.claim: Five named evidence packages remain open or blocked and gate any later launch, value, funding, or scale decision.
items.boundary: MODEL CONTROL PASS validates fail-closed behavior; it does not close client evidence gates.

items.claim: A 90-day evidence-mobilization timebox can prepare a separate stop, extend, or later bounded-pilot decision without authorizing execution.
items.evidence_label: ANALYST-JUDGMENT grounded in existing stage gates
items.boundary: The timebox is not a pilot duration or promise of closure; open evidence forces extension, redesign, or fallback.

chart_candidates.title: Weighted strategic-option score / 100
chart_candidates.annotation: Show seven gates separately; do not encode the scores as confidence or readiness.

open_questions: Will the Steering Committee confirm the federated direction and local fallback?
Who accepts accountability for each evidence package?
Can minimum integration readiness and a bottom-up initial-stage cost fit within the $1.0–$1.5m ceiling?
Which open evidence will require extension beyond the proposed 90-day mobilization timebox?
